missing: efficacy, new entry 3: year 2023, status contra, model 'BCMA+ myeloma xenografts (MM.1s intramedullary / escape model) in NSG mice', src https://doi.org/10.1136/jitc-2023-006699, srcLabel 'Lee 2023', PMID 37399355 / PMC10314698, J Immunother Cancer 11(6):e006699. Quote (abstract, verbatim): 'The APRIL CAR was well tolerated, but the clinical responses observed in AUTO2 were disappointing.' Lee 2018 (doi:10.1182/blood-2017-05-781351) predicted 'complete ACAR-mediated tumor clearance'; patients: 11 treated, 1 VGPR + 3 PR + 1 MR, terminated 'not sufficient to warrant further development' (NCT03287804, results first posted 2020-10-23, confirmed). Fields: subjects=patients, comparison_stated=true (paper traces the shortfall to reduced avidity/binding of cell-expressed APRIL that the xenograft never surfaced), epub/print 2023, registry_date 2020-10-23, product_in_model=true, magnitude=off_by_>5x (clearance vs 36% ORR, no CR), source_calls_it=miss. Fallback if the house takes the patient-side year: 2020 on the registry record, which rule 1 explicitly allows as a source.

safety, ADC arm (if the context is ever split by modality): EMA/CHMP/414341/2020 (23 July 2020) verbatim: 'In nonclinical toxicity studies, corneal effects (bilateral single cell necrosis in the corneal epithelium and/or increased mitoses of corneal epithelial cells) were seen in rats and rabbits, but not in monkeys.' Study dates: 13-week rat 2018N374327 and rabbit ocular 2018N385412 are 2018 as the drafter says, but the GLP 3-week rat study 2013N158643 already lists 'Non adverse changes in ... eyes' before DREAMM-1 (BMA117159, started 2014), so 'partly post hoc' overstates; the rat flagged the eye prospectively but called it non-adverse (direction matched, severity missed). This would be same/direction_only for the ADC arm, not contra.

engagement row 2: model_filed should be true, not null, for consistency with efficacy/safety rows citing the same FDA Abecma review (https://www.fda.gov/media/147627/download, section 4 'xenograft murine model'; verified).
rule_questions: Does a magnitude miss that ends in development termination count as contra, or only a direction reversal? The brief says 'predicted wrongly for a drug' and defines failure at the drug level ('went on to fail in patients'); the drafter's direction-only rule is its own invention. Checker's decision: contra (2023, Lee 2023 JITC). Consequence to decide: the same xenograft also predicted eradication for ide-cel (PFS 8.8 mo, no cures) and that is scored same/direction_only; the brief should state whether 'failed in patients' means development failure or direction reversal.

Can a registry record with no publication be the sole source for contra? Rule 1 lists 'a registry record' as a primary source, so yes; moot here because a peer-reviewed AUTO2 report exists (doi:10.1136/jitc-2023-006699).

Does structural model silence count as a wrong prediction when (a) the model could never show the toxicity (NSG, no human myeloid compartment), (b) the developers predicted it anyway from CD19 CAR experience and wrote it into the protocol (NCT02215967 detailed description), and (c) the model's one explicit safety prediction (plasma-cell-restricted BCMA expression, Carpenter 2013) held? The brief's 'best model = the one the class relied on for that question' argues the mouse was not the CRS model; its '(or its silence)' wording and the ad-amyloid precedent (species dosed, endpoint possible, nothing seen) argue contra. In ad-amyloid the species were actually asked; here the model was not. Needs a rule; checker left contra standing.

Mixed-modality class: 'BCMA-directed therapies - CAR-T, ADC, bispecifics' share an efficacy model but not safety or dose models (ADC: rat/rabbit/monkey tox, which did show cornea; bispecific: patient-marrow ex vivo + cyno; CAR-T: xenograft only). Should contra for one modality override the class, or should the context split by modality?

Rule 1 says the source must 'make the comparison', but both house examples (cf-cftr Ramsey 2011, ad-amyloid Egan 2019) accept drafter juxtaposition of a model paper and a patient paper (comparison_stated=false). Which governs? All three same/contra rows in this draft rely on juxtaposition; only the dose row is comparison_stated=true.
